chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Do not wear a garment that has buttons while you are in Ihram, except if you turn it inside out, nor a garment that you drape over your shoulders, nor trousers, except if you do not have an izar (loincloth), nor two socks, except if you do not have two shoes.
And I asked him about the one in Ihram who pairs between the clothes in which he entered Ihram and others. He said: There is no problem with that if they are clean.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.تَدَرَّعَهُ: To drape (a cloak over the shoulders)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for wearing buttons and multiple layers of clothing while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the specific prohibitions on wearing stitched garments (like trousers and buttoned tunics) for the Muhrim, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on simplicity and the removal of worldly adornment during pilgrimage. It further clarifies that mixing the original Ihram garments with other clean attire is permissible, highlighting the practical flexibility within the strictures of ritual purity and state of consecration.
